title: IAM roles and principals
summary: A principal is an identity asking for access. An IAM role groups permissions, and a policy binds a role to principals at a resource scope.
introduction: A principal is an identity asking for access. An IAM role groups permissions, and a policy binds a role to principals at a resource scope. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A principal is an identity asking for access. An IAM role groups permissions, and a policy binds a role to principals at a resource scope.

Scope: the intended practice resource
blocks.title: IAM roles and principals

blocks.text: The design gives a specific reader limited access. Choose the actual predefined role from the service guide.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why broad basic roles may grant more than a reviewer needs.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not grant owner access merely to bypass a permission error.
For more detail later, use this [Google Cloud Platform further reading](https://cloud.google.com/docs/overview).
